To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a novel regularisation approach for weight-fixing networks that can be used to train networks that use 1/3 the unique parameters of a baseline model, (2) we show that this approach can be used to compress a ResNet50 model to 56x fewer parameters, while achieving the same accuracy, (3) we demonstrate that the approach can be used in combination with a quantisation-aware training approach to further reduce the number of parameters by an order of magnitude
we have proposed a new approach for reducing the number of weights in a network, which is based on clustering the weights of the network.
we have designed a new network compression approach, which we call WFN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new way of thinking about the design of deep networks, and the implications of that design for energy efficiency and performance.
reducing the energy costs of inference calculations in deep learning accelerators.
the design of a network that can be stored on a PE array, and which is able to perform a task with a minimal number of weight updates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WFNs offer a promising new direction for low-energy deep learning.
WFNs are an effective way to reduce the number of unique values used by deep networks.
we show that the WFN approach is effective at reducing the unique weight count of a network, and the entropy of those weights.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the viability of a novel approach to weight sharing, which is able to achieve a significant reduction in the number of unique parameters in a network.
we show how to use the regularisation trick to achieve the best possible weight-space entropy for a network with the fewest unique weights.
we are able to achieve the same performance on Imagenet as the state-of-the-art quantisation techniques while using 56x less weights, and 1.9× lower weight-space entropy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a focus on weight-space entropy and unique weights is a viable route to low-entropy deep learning.
the energy costs of data movement dominate the energy costs for deep networks.

, in the absence of hardware support for weight reuse, the best way to reduce data-movement costs is by minimising the number of unique weight values, and that this can be achieved with a combination of simple, well-trodden techniques.
